_doc: Coefficients of the resource endowment and prospecting model (sim/geography/resources_*.py). Every entry is {id, value, unit, kind, source, conf, why}; sim/geography/parameters.py explains the kinds. All of these are heuristics until a geologic-province layer and a measured discovery history exist.

entries.source: Singer and Menzie 2010 and district sizes in research notes (mining districts tens to a few hundred km); [mem]
entries.why: Deposits cluster in metallogenic provinces; this is the e-fold distance of the boost a known deposit gives to its neighbours' expected counts.

entries.unit: multiplier per known deposit at zero distance
entries.source: none; chosen so a district's tile has several times the background density
entries.why: Strength of the provincial clustering kernel; refit against MRDS point density (Ripley K) when that data is loaded.
Upper bound on the density multiplier from clustering, so a dense catalogue cannot make a tile unboundedly rich.

entries.source: research notes section 7, step 4 (truncate at 3-4 sigma) [mem]
entries.why: Hidden deposit sizes are capped here: the rare giants beyond are the catalogue's, so they cannot be conjured where geology gives none.

entries.unit: variance to mean ratio of deposit counts
entries.source: research notes section 7, step 3 (variance 2-3 times the mean) [mem]
entries.why: Deposit counts are clustered, so more variable than Poisson; drawn as Poisson with a lognormal mean multiplier.

entries.source: research notes section 4 (top 3 km of crust) [mem]
entries.why: Depth of crust a pre-modern or early-modern working can plausibly touch; sets the crustal ceiling on a tile's undiscovered endowment.

entries.source: mean density of upper continental crust, standard reference value
entries.why: Converts a tile's area and depth to crustal mass for the ceiling.

entries.unit: fraction of crustal content that can be in ore
entries.source: research notes section 4: about 1e-6 to 1e-5 of crustal gold is in ore; ceiling set generously above that [mem]
entries.why: Hard ceiling: undiscovered endowment cannot exceed crustal abundance times mass times this fraction.

entries.unit: person-days of prospecting in a tile
entries.source: none; calibrate against the gold-rush discovery history (research notes section 3)
entries.why: Effort that finds a reference-sized, fully visible deposit with probability 1 - 1/e.
Deposit size that has discovery size factor 1.

entries.source: outcrop area scales as tonnage to the 0.3-0.5 power (research notes section 3) [mem]
entries.why: Bigger deposits show more at surface, so are found first (size-biased discovery).

entries.source: research notes section 7 step 6 (outcrop and placer 1, gossan vein 0.3-0.5, blind 0.05) [mem]
entries.why: How readily prospecting without geophysics turns up a deposit of each depth class.

entries.unit: fraction of tile area under the stand at full suitability
entries.source: none; used only when the forest_fraction layer is missing
entries.why: Cover of a biotic stand on a tile with no measured forest layer, scaled by the envelope suitability.
